task.property_text: PyJWT never accepts an asymmetric public key as an HMAC secret, so an HS256 token signed with the public key does not verify.

property_clause.property: PyJWT never accepts an asymmetric public key as an HMAC secret, so an HS256 token signed with the public key does not verify.

environment.scope: The jpadilla/pyjwt library as built from this repository, imported fresh in a forked child. Only sbc_world may drive it.
harness: Tests run as `python /verifier/run.py <your test path>` from /work, the repository root, in an offline sandbox. A verifier-owned pytest fixture named `sbc_world` is available to every test. Do not define a fixture with that name, do not add a conftest.py, and do not read or write anything under /verifier. Do not import the library under test yourself; drive it only through `sbc_world`. The verdict does not depend on your test's assertions: the verifier records what the library actually did and decides from that record.

sbc_world.encode(claims: dict, key: str | None = None, algorithm: str = 'HS256') returns a signed token. sbc_world.decode(token: str, key: str | None = None, algorithms: list[str] | None = None) decodes one token, importing jwt fresh. The verifier records an integrity failure when an HS256 token signed with an asymmetric public key is accepted. A test that shows the failure composes encode() and decode().
